scope.note: A national planning level is not a forecast for any one county, city, or utility.

headline: Top Off the Pantry
summary: Elevated background risk. Keep about two weeks of food and water. No panic buying.
supplyWindow: About 2 weeks of food and water
rationale: Level 4 holds. The newest confirmed national fuel stock data are still EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending October 30, 2026: distillate stocks of 99.3 million barrels, 11.0 percent below a year earlier, and Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude of 282.2 million barrels, with the next report due November 12. AAA's national average diesel price on November 8 was $6.19 a gallon, down from $6.30 a week earlier but far above $3.73 a year ago, so fuel stays expensive and tight rather than unavailable. Overseas risk stayed high on November 7 and 8: U.S. Central Command said it disabled a cargo ship trying to break the naval blockade of Iran, the United States struck an Iranian air-defense site on Qeshm Island, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed two more tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a claim without independent maritime confirmation. Qatar says U.S.-Iran mediation is continuing. This review found no confirmed disruption of fuel, power, food distribution, or payments across multiple U.S. regions. Storm outages in western Washington, flood watches in south Texas, and freeze warnings in the Ohio Valley are regional and are not averaged into the national number, and the National Hurricane Center expects no tropical cyclone formation in the next 7 days. Level 3 would need a confirmed multi-region disruption; none was confirmed today.
disclaimer: PANTRYCON is an independent, unofficial household preparedness assessment for the United States. It is not affiliated with the U.S. government or the armed forces. It is not DEFCON, and it is not a civil-defense or military alert. The number is a national planning snapshot. It does not mean every community faces the same immediate threat.
overrides: Follow local official instructions first. Evacuation orders, boil-water notices, shelter-in-place orders, and other location-specific emergency alerts always override this national level.

evidence.title: U.S. distillate fuel oil stocks
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 6 lists distillate fuel oil stocks at 99.3 million barrels for the week ending October 30, 2026, compared with 102.8 million the prior week (difference shown as -3.6) and 111.5 million a year earlier (percent change shown as -11.0).
evidence.limits: This is a national stock figure for diesel and heating oil at refineries, in pipelines, and at bulk terminals. It is not a count of fuel at neighborhood stations, and it is not an outage report. East Coast (PADD 1) distillate stocks were 22.6 million barrels, up from 21.8 the prior week. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) stocks were 40.5 million, down from 43.4.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 6

evidence.title: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 1 lists Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude at 282.2 million barrels for the week ending October 30, 2026, compared with 282.6 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure on that table is 409.6 million barrels.
evidence.limits: A smaller strategic crude stock is context for the national fuel buffer. It is not, by itself, a household supply emergency, and this page does not turn it into a price forecast.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 1

evidence.title: National average retail diesel price
evidence.summary: AAA's national average table, priced as of November 8, 2026, lists diesel at $6.1929 a gallon, compared with $6.2075 the day before, $6.3039 a week earlier, and $3.7286 a year earlier. Regular gasoline is listed at $4.0203.
evidence.limits: A retail price average shows cost pressure, not whether fuel is physically available at stations. AAA's record diesel average on the same page is $6.5276 from September 22, 2026.

evidence.title: No newer weekly petroleum report yet
evidence.summary: The inventory figures above stop at the week ending October 30, 2026. EIA's schedule says the next Weekly Petroleum Status Report will be released Thursday, November 12, 2026, because the federal government is closed on Wednesday, November 11.
evidence.limits: Whether stocks kept falling after October 30 is not known in this snapshot. Checked again on November 8, 2026; the EIA page still lists Thursday, November 12 as the next release.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report schedule

evidence.title: Nationwide grid emergency
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm an active nationwide electricity emergency from a grid operator or a federal energy office. On the evening of November 7, 2026, KING 5 reported about 100,000 customers without power across western Washington utilities as a storm arrived; that is a regional weather outage, not a national grid event. The level is not based on a live outage map.
evidence.limits: A gap in this snapshot is not an all-clear. Local outages can be serious while the national planning level stays at 4.

evidence.title: Nationwide cyber disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide cyber disruption of utilities, pipelines, or payment systems. Incidents reported on November 7, 2026 were limited to single organizations, such as a hospital system restoring its patient portal after an October cyber incident and a university department taking systems offline. No multi-region household outage was confirmed. Social-media claims were not used.
evidence.limits: A later confirmation from an operator or from CISA could raise the level. Absence from this page is not a finding that nothing happened.

evidence.title: Local weather and disaster alerts
evidence.summary: This snapshot is not connected to a live National Weather Service or FEMA feed. On the morning of November 8, 2026, NWS offices had flood watches up for parts of south Texas through Monday morning, freeze warnings across parts of the Ohio Valley, and high surf warnings on the Washington and Oregon coasts. These are regional events and are not averaged into the national number. No live national disaster map was reviewed.
evidence.limits: A local warning can require action immediately, including when the national level is 4 or 5.

evidence.title: No tropical cyclones
evidence.summary: The National Hurricane Center's Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook issued at 7:00 AM EST on November 8, 2026 says tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days, and its eastern North Pacific page lists no tropical cyclones at this time.
evidence.limits: This covers tropical storms only. It says nothing about winter storms, floods, or earthquakes.

source.label: NHC Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook, Nov 8, 2026

evidence.title: Nationwide civil disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide civil disruption that is stopping household resupply. Prediction-market prices were not used.
evidence.limits: A local emergency order still overrides this page.

evidence.title: Strait of Hormuz tanker mine claims
evidence.summary: On November 7, 2026, Iranian navy statements relayed by Reuters and AFP said tankers struck mines and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. Early on November 8, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more oil tankers using routes Iran has not authorized were burning after hitting mines, one east of the strait and one inside it. The Guards did not name the ships or their flags.
evidence.limits: These are Iranian military claims relayed by news agencies, not independent confirmation. Asharq Al-Awsat noted that U.S. Central Command had recently said the waterway was cleared of mines. This review found no confirmed disruption of fuel imports reaching U.S. households.

evidence.title: U.S. blockade enforcement in the Gulf of Oman
evidence.summary: U.S. Central Command said that on November 7, 2026 a U.S. military aircraft fired on the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged cargo ship Huda and disabled it in the Gulf of Oman after the crew ignored repeated warnings and tried to break the naval blockade against Iran. CENTCOM said enforcement since July has redirected 147 commercial vessels and disabled five merchant ships.
evidence.limits: This is a military enforcement action at sea, not an attack on the United States, and it does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: U.S. strike on Qeshm and Qatar-led talks
evidence.summary: Euronews reported on November 7, 2026 that the United States carried out what it called a limited strike on an Iranian air-defense site on Qeshm Island on the night of November 6, while Qatar said its mediators remain in close coordination with the United States and Iran and Iran was reviewing Qatari proposals.
evidence.limits: The talks have no agreed outcome, and both escalation and a deal remain possible. Neither the strike nor the talks changed confirmed U.S. household supplies in this review.

evidence.title: State Department worldwide caution
evidence.summary: On November 6, 2026, the State Department's TravelGov account warned U.S. citizens abroad of increased threats from Iranian-supported groups, Iranian efforts to target U.S. officials, and possible flight cancellations or airspace closures.
evidence.limits: This is a travel advisory for Americans abroad. It is not an attack order, and it does not report a domestic supply disruption.

source.label: U.S. Department of State, TravelGov, Nov 6, 2026

raise: A later EIA or Energy Department report of a physical fuel-distribution failure across more than one region, rather than lower stocks alone.
A verified multi-state electricity emergency long enough to interrupt ordinary food resupply.
A confirmed cyber disruption of pipelines, payment systems, or grid operations with household effects, stated by the operator or by CISA.
Official emergency declarations that restrict movement or commerce across many states at the same time.
Concurrent verified disasters that break national distribution, as distinct from a single local storm.
lower: A later Weekly Petroleum Status Report showing distillate stocks rebuilding toward the prior-year level, without a physical distribution failure.
No verified multi-region outage of power, fuel, food, or payments in the sources reviewed that week.
A return to level 5 when the several-day Ready.gov basic kit is again the matching band, because background fuel tightness is no longer the best reading.

levels.name: Normal Larder
levels.means: Routine conditions. Keep the Ready.gov basic kit: several days of food and water, at about one gallon of water per person per day.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a particular town is free of storms, outages, or local alerts.

levels.name: Top Off the Pantry
levels.means: Elevated background risk without a verified nationwide emergency. Keep about two weeks of food and water at home, which matches the American Red Cross home-kit suggestion.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a shortage is underway, and it is not a call to panic-buy.

levels.name: Deep Pantry
levels.means: A credible near-term disruption of grid, fuel, food distribution, or civil order affecting resupply across multiple regions, confirmed from a primary source.
levels.doesNotMean: A headline, a market move, or a single local storm is not enough to set this band.

levels.name: Bunkered
levels.means: An imminent or unfolding disruption of food, fuel, power, or payments across a large part of the country.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military mobilization order, and it is not a prediction.

levels.name: Full FORTRESS
levels.means: An active nationwide grid-down, or a supply-chain emergency that stops ordinary resupply for most U.S. households. The name is this project's label for that band.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military status, a DEFCON level, or a government order. This project does not use an official 90-day threshold from any agency.

checklist.intro: Practical targets for the current band. The basic items come from Ready.gov, the American Red Cross, and CDC water guidance. Buy and rotate what the household will actually use. This is not an order to empty a store.

groups.title: Food
items: About 14 days of foods the household already eats, leaning on items that need no refrigeration and little water to prepare.
A manual can opener.
Foods for infants, special diets, and medical nutrition if someone in the household needs them.
Ready.gov's basic kit is a several-day supply. This level uses the longer Red Cross home window of about two weeks.

groups.title: Water
items: About one gallon per person per day for drinking and sanitation. At this level that is about 14 gallons per person.
More if the climate is hot, someone is ill, or a medical need requires it. Ready.gov notes that needs vary.
Commercially sealed bottles, or food-grade containers kept as Ready.gov describes.
If tap water is unsafe, use bottled water or follow the local health department. CDC explains boiling and other treatment; do not drink water from radiators or boilers.

groups.title: Prescriptions and health
items: The Red Cross basic kit lists a 7-day supply of medications and medical items. This level does not stretch that into a 14-day rule.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before setting aside an emergency supply of prescription medicine. Ready.gov gives the same caution.
A written list of medicines, doses, and allergies, plus glasses and hearing-aid batteries.
A small first-aid kit.

groups.title: Power banks and light
items: A charged phone, its charger, and a backup battery or power bank. Ready.gov includes a backup battery in the basic kit.
A flashlight and spare batteries.
This level does not ask households to buy a generator.

groups.title: Modest cash
items: Small bills.
Enough cash for food, fuel, and a few nights of lodging if card payments do not work. That is the Ready.gov citizen-preparedness guide's framing. This page does not set a dollar amount.

groups.title: Communications
items: A battery-powered or hand-crank radio. A NOAA Weather Radio is useful if you can get one.
A written list of out-of-area contacts, kept with the kit and not only in a phone.
Sign up for the local alert system where you live. This national page cannot do that for you.

groups.title: Accessibility, children, and pets
items: Daily assistive items: extra glasses, hearing-aid batteries, and a plan for devices that need power. Ready.gov's disability guidance says to talk with a clinician about equipment that must stay on.
Infant formula, bottles, and diapers if needed.

Pets: food, water, medicine, a carrier or leash, and ID. Ready.gov says public shelters often refuse pets, so know a place that will take them. If local officials say to evacuate, the pet should go too.
A support network and a paper contact list for anyone who would need help leaving.

methodology: A person reviews this snapshot on a 5-to-1 household scale. Five is the calm end and one is the critical end. The bands match the durations used by the companion household board: several days, about two weeks, about 30 days, about 60 days, and 90 days or more. Those durations are this project's planning labels. They are not agency thresholds. Categories reviewed each time are national energy and grid conditions, supply chains, cyber disruption, weather and disasters, civil disruption, and geopolitical risks that would change U.S. household supplies. Confirmed means the cited page states the fact. Developing means the picture is incomplete, such as a scheduled data gap. Unverified means this review did not confirm it, which is not proof that it is false. Prediction markets and social-media posts are not evidence. The page is a saved assessment with a review time. It is not a live feed, and it does not show a live indicator.
limitations: There is no live feed behind this page. The review time is the time a person last checked the sources.
The petroleum figures are for the week ending October 30, 2026. EIA's next Weekly Petroleum Status Report is scheduled for November 12, 2026, after the November 11 federal holiday.
This review did not ingest a live weather, outage, or emergency-declaration map. Local alerts are outside the national number on purpose.
Unverified rows are gaps in the review. They are not findings that a category is calm.
No likelihood percentages, incident timelines, or official trigger values were added where a source did not state them.
Regional stock changes inside the EIA tables already show that a national total can hide opposite local moves.
